title: MLB Velo Bands
headline_insight: The median four-seam fastball in the 2025 pull sits at 94.5 mph, with 34.78% of four-seamers landing in the 95-98 mph band and 8.0% in 98-101.
what_it_means: The modern fastball is genuinely fast: a third of four-seamers reach 95-98 mph and another 8% cross 98. Breaking and off-speed pitches live far lower on the scale, sliders around 86.4 mph and curveballs around 79.9. Velocity also ramps up over the season, the four-seam median rising 0.4 mph from a 94.2 April to a 94.6 September.
how_to_read: The band table gives each pitch type's share across mph buckets; the monthly section tracks median velocity by month to show the in-season ramp.
why_it_matters: It is the descriptive velocity landscape of a full season of pitches, the raw distribution behind any stuff or velo-based work.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY; in-season velo ramp-up is a known physical effect reported as-is. Thin edge-of-season months (Mar/Oct) fall below the per-cell floor and vanish. Nothing here is modeled, forecast or priced.
as_of: 2025 Statcast season pull (no generation timestamp in artifact)
